stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to a large prisoner swap; US envoys go on to Moscow to meet Putin
stories.summary: Two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended Wednesday with Russia and Ukraine agreeing to a large exchange of prisoners of war but no wider agreement on ending the war. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Thursday to meet Vladimir Putin and are due to see Volodymyr Zelensky afterward. Zelensky said on Thursday that new restrictions on the Starshield satellite service are hampering Ukraine's forces along the front.
stories.why_it_matters: The swap would bring prisoners home on both sides, but the talks did not produce a ceasefire, so the fighting and the strikes on Ukraine's power grid continue heading into winter. The outcome also shapes how much Europe and the US will keep spending on the war and on their own defense.
stories.background: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine is nearly five years old. The Trump administration has been mediating direct talks between the two sides, led by envoy Steve Witkoff and the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner; an earlier round in Abu Dhabi this year also produced a prisoner exchange without a broader settlement. Russia wants the talks to cover European security arrangements, while Ukraine says progress depends on how the US deals with Moscow. Separately, Ukraine has complained since mid-October that SpaceX's military satellite service, Starshield, has been throttled for its forces. Leaders of more than 40 European countries are meeting in Dublin on Thursday to discuss the continent's security.

facts.text: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war, both sides said Wednesday, as two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a major breakthrough on ending the war.
Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov described the agreed exchange as "large-scale" and said negotiators were returning to their capitals to finalize details.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Zelensky said Ukrainian units had recorded new and significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite service in recent days along the entire front line, and said this was helping Russia carry out more accurate strikes.
Zelensky said progress in the peace talks depends on the US approach to Russia.
Russia struck six major power substations on Nov. 11, causing outages across Ukraine, the Kyiv Independent reported.
Leaders from more than 40 European countries gathered in Dublin on Thursday for a European Political Community summit focused on the continent's security.
France said the EU will approve more sanctions on Russia on Monday.
The New York Times reported that US envoys urged Russia to include Europe in the talks, as the Kremlin seeks discussions on European security structures.

stories.headline: Israeli airstrike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital kills at least six, health officials say
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza overnight, killing at least six people, including a surgeon, according to Gaza's health ministry. Israel said it carried out a precise strike on a Hamas commander and a command center operating inside the hospital complex. Hamas called the strike an attack on a civilian medical facility.
stories.why_it_matters: Nasser is the largest hospital in southern Gaza, and the strike comes while a ceasefire described as increasingly fragile is in place. In this digest the story was carried by left-leaning and center outlets; no right-leaning outlet covered it.
stories.background: Nasser Hospital is the largest hospital in southern Gaza and, according to a doctor quoted by the Guardian, one of the few medical facilities still operating in the territory. It has been hit before during the war between Israel and Hamas, including strikes in 2025 that prompted United Nations calls for an investigation. Israel says Hamas uses the hospital complex for military purposes; Hamas describes it as a civilian medical facility. Casualty figures in Gaza come from the health ministry, which is run by Hamas, and from rescue services. A ceasefire is in effect, though Deutsche Welle describes it as increasingly fragile.

Israel said the target was the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, the Times of Israel reported.

stories.headline: Spain holds its first general strike in 14 years over housing costs; clashes follow in Barcelona and Madrid
stories.summary: Workers across Spain walked off the job Wednesday in a 24-hour general strike called by the main unions over housing costs and the cost of living, the country's first in 14 years. Large evening protests followed in Madrid and Barcelona, where some protesters clashed with police. The strike comes less than three weeks before a snap election on Nov. 29.
stories.why_it_matters: Rents and home prices have become the central issue in an election that could change Spain's government, and the turnout is being read as a measure of public anger. Housing affordability is a pressure point in many countries, not only Spain.
stories.background: Rising rents and stagnant wages have become central issues in Spain, and protests over housing have been building for weeks. In early October a housing march in Barcelona ended in clashes with police, and the government approved urgent housing measures the next day. The housing crisis led to a snap general election being called for Nov. 29, in which Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is expected to face a strong challenge from the right. The country's main unions called Wednesday's strike over housing and the cost of living.

facts.text: Spain held its first general strike in 14 years on Wednesday, a 24-hour stoppage over housing costs.

Protesters in Barcelona set fires and launched fireworks at riot police on Paseo de Gracia, Fox News reported.

stories.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases as Kenya discharges its last patient
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 11,000 cases and 5,387 deaths, and the medical charity Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Thursday it is still out of control six months on. Kenya, which had nine confirmed cases, discharged its last patient on Wednesday and began a 42-day countdown to being declared free of the virus.
stories.why_it_matters: This is the deadliest Ebola outbreak Congo has recorded, and it has already crossed borders. Kenya's progress suggests neighbors can contain imported cases, but MSF says the source outbreak is not under control.
stories.background: Ebola is a severe and often fatal viral disease. Congo declared its 17th outbreak in May, though experts believe the virus was circulating weeks or months earlier. Authorities have struggled to contain it because of armed conflict and a health system in crisis. A small number of cases reached neighboring countries, including Kenya, which now starts a 42-day count toward being declared Ebola-free if no new cases appear.

facts.text: Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 11,000 cases and is the country's deadliest.
The outbreak has caused 5,387 deaths, the Hindu reported.

MSF said large sums of international aid are not reaching the front line, according to RFI.
Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient and began a 42-day countdown to being declared free of the disease, provided no new cases are recorded.
Kenya had nine confirmed cases.
The Committee to Protect Journalists said attacks and threats against journalists in Congo have risen, driven in part by a backlash against reporting on the outbreak.

stories.headline: Hoax bomb threats hit schools in Italy, the UK and Ireland after a wave of threats against flights
stories.summary: Schools across Italy were evacuated Wednesday after bomb threats that authorities treated as hoaxes, and similar threats reached schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and Ireland. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no sign of concrete danger and that the threats were meant to spread alarm. Reuters cited a report of more Italian school evacuations on Thursday.
stories.why_it_matters: No bombs have been found, but the threats have emptied classrooms and disrupted flights for thousands of people. Authorities have not publicly identified who is behind them.
stories.background: Europe has seen a run of hoax bomb alerts in recent weeks, including against passenger flights, alongside cyberattacks. In early November an anonymous email claiming to come from Iran's Revolutionary Guards was sent to hundreds of Italian schools; Italian authorities have not confirmed who sent it. Some outlets describe the pattern as possible hybrid warfare, meaning disruption short of armed attack. Authorities in Italy, the UK and Ireland say there appears to be no risk to the public.

stories.headline: Indonesia's vice president, son of former leader Jokowi, resigns over school credentials
stories.summary: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka formally submitted his resignation on Thursday after court rulings found that the education documents he filed to run for office did not meet election requirements. Gibran, 39, is the eldest son of former President Joko Widodo. President Prabowo Subianto must now settle on a successor.
stories.why_it_matters: The resignation ends the alliance between Indonesia's current president and his predecessor that brought the government to office. Who replaces Gibran will show how much power Prabowo now holds on his own.
stories.background: Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, is the eldest son of former President Joko Widodo, known as Jokowi. His place as vice president was a symbol of the partnership between Jokowi and Prabowo Subianto that carried Prabowo into the presidency. Last month the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled that documents he submitted about his overseas schooling did not meet election requirements, and calls for him to step down grew. Parliament had been preparing to take up his position when he resigned.

facts.text: Gibran handed his resignation to parliament on Thursday.
The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that documents Gibran submitted about his overseas education did not meet election requirements.
Gibran had filed a certificate saying his overseas education was equivalent to an Indonesian vocational high school, the Japan Times reported.
Joko Widodo voiced support for Prabowo as his son resigned.
Prabowo said the resignation was "for greater good," Nikkei Asia reported.

stories.headline: Russia's ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, dies at 66
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry announced Wednesday that Alexander Darchiev, Moscow's ambassador to Washington, had died at 66. The first statement said he died suddenly and gave no cause; the ministry later attributed the death to a chronic illness. No successor has been named in the coverage.
stories.why_it_matters: Darchiev was Moscow's main diplomatic channel in Washington while the two governments negotiate over the war in Ukraine. His death leaves that post empty during active talks.
stories.background: Alexander Darchiev was a long-time diplomat who took up the Washington post in early 2025, as relations between the Kremlin and the Trump White House warmed. He had earlier served as Russia's ambassador to Canada. Fox News described his assignment as leading a rapprochement with the Trump administration. His death was announced the same day US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine ended in Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV returns to Peru, where he spent two decades, and is met by large crowds
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Lima on Wednesday to begin a visit to Peru, the country where he worked for two decades as a missionary and bishop and holds citizenship. He called Peru his homeland and was received by President Keiko Fujimori. The visit, the last stop of a three-country Latin American tour, includes Chiclayo, the city where he served as bishop.
stories.why_it_matters: The visit is a national event in Peru and shows the personal ties between the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics and Latin America. In this digest it was covered by left-leaning and center outlets only.
stories.background: Leo XIV, 71, leads the world's 1.4 billion Catholics. Before his election he spent about two decades in Peru as a missionary and later as bishop of the northern city of Chiclayo, and he became a Peruvian citizen. Peru is the final leg of a three-nation Latin American trip. The New York Times noted that he was welcomed by President Keiko Fujimori, whose father's policies he had protested.

facts.text: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Lima on Wednesday and called Peru his "homeland."
An estimated 3 million people greeted him in Lima at the start of a six-day visit, Deutsche Welle reported.

Peru is the last leg of a three-nation Latin American tour for the 71-year-old pope.
